text: dsh-speed（DSH 插件，Web 与终端客户端）：为 OpenAI、Codex 及配置的代理模型提供 Standard、Fast 和 Ultrafast 速度选择。它在 Web 模型选择区加入速度选择器，并提供终端 /speed 命令；根据模型与账户目录展示可用档位，将会话、提供方和模型对应的选择应用到后续请求。适合希望按会话调整 DSH 模型速度的用户。Codex 路由需已有本机 Codex 登录；OpenAI 使用 DSH 已配置的凭据。

dsh-speed adds Standard, Fast, and Ultrafast choices for supported OpenAI, Codex, and configured proxy models. Web users select a tier in model controls; terminal users run /speed. Available tiers depend on the model and account. Codex uses an existing local sign-in; OpenAI uses DSH credentials.
想给 DSH 当前会话切换 Fast 或 Ultrafast 模式。
怎么在 DSH 网页模型选择栏里选速度档位？
I want to choose a faster tier for a DSH model session.
dsh-speed 的功能「Web 速度选择器」：在对话输入区的模型控件中显示当前模型可用的 Standard、Fast 或 Ultrafast 档位，并可刷新档位列表和保存选择。
dsh-speed 的功能「终端速度命令」：在终端使用 /speed 打开档位选择，或输入 status、standard、fast、ultrafast 查看或设置当前会话的速度。设置仅在 agent 空闲且该模型支持所选档位时保存。
dsh-speed 使用前须知：Codex 路由读取本机登录信息并向 chatgpt.com 查询账户模型目录；OpenAI 路由使用 DSH 已配置凭据。（见 lib/catalog.js:8-19、index.js:68-70）

dsh-speed README · dsh-speed：Fast and Ultrafast for DSH web, terminal commands, and agent model requests. Managed source: [nix-config/pkgs/dsh-speed](https://github.com/jakehemmerle/nix-config/tree/main/pkgs/dsh-speed).

dsh-speed README · Use：Open the existing **Model / Effort** menu and choose **Speed**: Standard, Fast, or Ultrafast. In `dst`, `/speed` opens an arrow-key picker when all three speeds are available; use Up/Down and Enter, or Escape to cancel. With only Standard and Fast available it toggles between them. `/speed status` reports the current choice, and `/speed standard`, `/speed fast`, `/speed ultrafast` set it directly. The start screen and bottom bar display `Speed: Standard`, `Speed: ⚡` (Fast), or `Speed: ⚡⚡` (Ultrafast). Changes apply to subsequent requests. A web selection during streaming leaves the active request unchanged; the terminal command requires an idle agent.

dsh-speed README · Use：Selections are independent for each session, provider, and model. Titles and other auxiliary requests do not inherit the conversational speed. Teammates start with their own Standard selection; their authentication still uses the same configured provider. A parent's Fast or Ultrafast setting never silently spills into a teammate.

dsh-speed README · Use：| Route | Credential source | Speed availability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local `openai-codex` | Local Codex `auth.json` | That account's native model catalog |
| Configured `providerproxy` | ProviderProxy client key | Proxy `/v1/models` catalog |
| Official `openai` API | Existing DSH API credential | Explicit supported-model list / configured opt-ins |

dsh-speed README · Use：**Fast sends `priority`; Ultrafast sends `ultrafast`.** Native requests also send Codex's `x-codex-routing-hint`. Standard sends `default` after explicitly selecting it. Before selection the existing transport defaults apply.

dsh-speed README · Authentication and configuration：Managed profiles read `~/.codex/auth.json` directly for local Codex requests, including agents. They do not copy refresh tokens into DSH's credential store. Reads follow the current file so an account switch takes effect on the next request. Near expiry, the configured Codex executable refreshes its own login through `account/read`; DSH then rereads the file. Missing or invalid native credentials fail visibly. Use `codex login` if that device has never signed in.

dsh-speed README · Authentication and configuration：ProviderProxy is a separate credential plane. The launcher reads its client key from the managed token file; the proxy owns and refreshes its upstream OAuth login. Local Codex tokens are never forwarded to the proxy. Only an explicitly configured provider with the exact allowed base URL can receive proxy speed options.

Example host-entry configuration:

```yaml
- id: dsh-speed
  name: /absolute/path/to/dsh-speed/index.js
  config:
    codexAuthFile: /home/you/.codex/auth.json

dsh-speed README · Authentication and configuration：Use the managed Nix profile to upgrade; do not install a duplicate row. DSH must restart to load a new host plugin. The Model/Effort child slot is a checked build-time patch to pinned DSH 0.2.1-alpha.2. Runtime transport compatibility is audited for pi-ai 0.87.1 and 1.1.0; other versions fail rather than silently ignoring speed.

dsh-speed README · Authentication and configuration：The native catalog caches for five minutes and the proxy catalog for one minute, keyed by credentials. Refresh forces a new catalog read. Unknown models, unavailable credentials, and failed catalogs expose only Standard. A revoked saved tier warns and rejects generation until a valid speed is selected.

dsh-speed README · Authentication and configuration：Preferences default to `~/.dsh/dsh-speed.json.d/`, one atomically replaced 0600 record per session/provider/model in a 0700 directory. Independent web and terminal processes cannot overwrite unrelated records. Existing array-format `dsh-speed.json` is a read-only migration fallback. `stateFile: false` uses memory only.

dsh-speed README · Authentication and configuration：Accelerated access depends on the selected account and may consume more allowance or cost more. A work account may advertise Fast without Ultrafast. The plugin cannot grant entitlement. Reported response tiers may differ from requested tiers even in the native Codex client; request parity proves correct protocol use, not a latency or billing guarantee.

dsh-speed README · Tests：The Nix derivation runs unit, property, client, runtime, and pinned-bundle contract tests. The real DSH E2E suite uses an isolated HOME, workspace, port, and tmux socket with synthetic HTTP credentials. It exercises native and proxy routes, six model/tier combinations, browser persistence and isolation, busy states, narrow layout, terminal commands, and Team delegation.

dsh-speed README · Tests：```sh
DSH_PI_AI_MODULE=/path/to/host/pi-ai/dist/index.js \
DSH_MODEL_BUNDLE=/path/to/unpatched/model-selection/lib/client.js npm test

DSH_BIN=/path/to/patched/dsh CHROMIUM_PATH=/path/to/chrome npm run test:e2e

dsh-speed README · Tests：All real-account tests are gated. `npm test` and `npm run test:e2e` use only synthetic credentials and loopback HTTP mocks. Direct live-runner invocation refuses before reading credentials unless `--live` or `DSH_LIVE_TESTS=1` is supplied. Real agent E2E additionally requires `DSH_LIVE_AGENTS=1`; run it only deliberately with `npm run test:live:agents`.

Real-account smoke tests consume plan allowance. From the nix-config root:

dsh-speed README · Tests：```sh
python3 -B tests/test_dsh_speed.py "$(command -v dsh)" --live --all-tiers
python3 -B tests/test_dsh_speed.py "$(command -v dsh)" --live --provider providerproxy --all-tiers
```

dsh-speed README · Tests：Native tests use the actual local auth bridge with an empty DSH credential store. Proxy tests use the same managed token file as the launcher. They save selections through the public handler, inspect the final HTTP payload, require a successful terminal response and `SPEED_OK`, and report requested and returned tiers separately. Unsupported account tiers are reported explicitly. Timing is diagnostic, not a benchmark.

dsh-speed README · Native protocol evidence：**Native comparison, 2026-10-10, bundled Codex CLI 0.160.1:** isolated real CLI runs using the same local OAuth login completed all six model/mode combinations with `SPEED_OK`. A loopback proxy scoped only to those CLI processes captured the actual WebSocket requests to `wss://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`; the running desktop app and system trust store were unchanged. The native wire contract was:

dsh-speed README · Native protocol evidence：| Mode | `response.create.service_tier` | `x-codex-routing-hint` on the WebSocket handshake |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | omitted | `model=<model>` |
| Fast | `priority` | `model=<model>;tier=priority` |
| Ultrafast | `ultrafast` | `model=<model>;tier=ultrafast` |

dsh-speed README · Native protocol evidence：Both `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6-astra` accepted Ultrafast through the native CLI. Every actual generation, including native Fast and Ultrafast, nevertheless reported `service_tier: "default"` in `response.completed`. Native connection prewarming used `generate: false` and reported `auto`; those events are not generations. Adding the native routing header to the DSH SSE probe did not change its reported tier. Therefore the strict tier-confirmation failures above also occur with the native client; they do not establish that DSH was downgraded or that acceleration occurred. Compare request parity separately from latency/throughput and billing evidence.

dsh-speed README · Native protocol evidence：To reproduce a native Sol Ultrafast smoke test using the CLI's existing login (substitute `gpt-6-astra` for Astra):

```sh
codex --no-daemon --disable apps --disable plugins exec \
  --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check \
  -s read-only -m gpt-6.1-sol \
  -c 'service_tier="ultrafast"' -c 'model_reasoning_effort="low"' \
